newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Ousted Afghan government attacks pass to Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Afghan government attacks pass to Kabul.

text.p: Forces belonging to the ousted Afghan government launched an attack on Sunday using rockets, artillery and planes in a bid to take a strategic pass from the Taleban in Kabul.

"We are very busy now," said General Abdul Rauf Begi, commander of forces on the frontline belonging to northern Uzbek leader Abdul Rashid Dostum, now allied to former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
Begi, a Russian map spread out before him, directed shells and rockets onto Taleban positions in the barren hills below the De Sabz pass north of Kabul.
One of Masood's commanders, Sayid Akbar, said two planes belonging to Dostum bombed Taleban positions on the hill early on Sunday morning.

He said the attack began at 6.00 a.m (0130 GMT) and there appeared to be little or no return fire from the Taleban. Positions around a second pass leading to Kabul, Khair Khana, were said by commanders to be quiet.
The allied forces are battling the Islamic Taleban movement, which swept into Kabul last month forcing Masood to retreat to the hills north of the capital.
